title_en: The Ruling on the Fund Popularly Known as al-Kīṣ
body_ar: السلام عليكم ورحمة الله تعالى وبركاته بالنسبة للصندوق الذي تعارف الناس عليه وهو أن يجمع عدد من الناس مالا يجمع بينهم بالسوية كل واحد منهم يدفع مبلغا وعلى قدر ذلك المبلغ يدفع الآخرون فيكون المال بالاشتراك والسوية بينهم ثم يقرضونه لأحدهم كل شهر إذا رده أخذه الآخر وهكذا بالتناوب سواء كان ذلك باتفاق مقدم أو كان بالقرعة أو كان بحسب ما يعرض لهم من الأزمات أو كان بحسب الطلبات في كل شهر يجتمعون فيقدمون أحوجهم هذا كله سلف جر نفعا لأن كل واحد منهم ما دفع ألفا إلا ليسف ثلاثين ألفا أو يسلف المبلغ الذي يطلبه فهو يسلف هذه الألف ليسلف أكثر منها وأسلفني على أن أسلفك أم من أمها الربا فيعتبر هذا سلفا جر نفعا والقرض لابد أن يكون لوجه لله ولا يحل للإنسان أن ينتفع به في الدنيا بل لا بد أن يفعله ابتغاء مرضاة الله. أسأل الله سبحانه وتعالى أن يغفر لنا أجمعين وأن يغنينا بحلاله عن حرامه وبطاعته عن معصيته وبفضله عن من سواه والسلام عليكم ورحمة الله. اضغط هنا لمشاهدة الفتوى
body_en:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God the Exalted and His blessings.

As regards the fund that people have come to know among themselves — that is, that a number of people pool money between them in equal shares, each one of them paying in a sum, and the others paying to the measure of that sum, so that the money is held jointly and equally among them; then each month they lend it to one of them, and when he has returned it another takes it, and so on in rotation, whether that is by prior agreement, or by drawing lots, or according to whatever emergencies befall them, or according to the requests made each month when they meet and give precedence to the neediest among them — all of this is a loan that has drawn a benefit. For not one of them has paid in a thousand except in order to be lent thirty thousand, or to be lent the sum he asks for; so he lends out this thousand in order to be lent more than it. And "lend me on condition that I lend you" is one of the mother-cases of usurious gain (ribā). So this counts as a loan that has drawn a benefit.

A loan must be for God's sake, and it is not lawful for a person to derive a worldly benefit from it; rather he must do it seeking God's good pleasure.

I ask God, glorified and exalted, to forgive us all, and to enrich us by what He has made lawful so that we need nothing He has forbidden, and by obedience to Him so that we need no disobedience, and by His bounty so that we need no one besides Him. And peace be upon you, and the mercy of God.

flags.note: This is the worked example in style guide section 5 and the recommended rendering there is kept. Mauritanian dialect term for a rotating savings and credit association; Malaysian readers know the structure as 'kutu' or 'committee'. The title is left with the transliterated local name because the Sheikh himself presents it as the popular name, and the body then describes the structure in full, so the English reader is not left guessing. The Sheikh's office should still confirm the intended structure before a fixed rendering is chosen corpus-wide.

flags.context: هذا كله سلف جر نفعا … فيعتبر هذا سلفا جر نفعا
options: a loan that has drawn a benefit
a loan bringing a benefit to the lender
flags.note: The phrase is the classical formula (كل قرض جر نفعا فهو ربا). 'A loan that has drawn a benefit' keeps it as the term of art it is. It must not be rendered 'interest-bearing': the Sheikh's point is precisely that no interest is charged here and the arrangement is still caught, because the benefit is the reciprocal lending.

flags.context: ما دفع ألفا إلا ليسف ثلاثين ألفا
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): dropped letter. The parallel clause immediately after has يسلف, which settles the reading. Preserved unchanged in body_ar.

flags.context: وأسلفني على أن أسلفك أم من أمها الربا
options: read as أمٌّ من أمهات الربا, 'one of the mother-cases of usurious gain'
read as 'a mother case whose mother is ribā'
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): أمها appears to stand for أمهات. The first reading is the established idiom and is what the sentence requires. Preserved unchanged in body_ar.

translator_notes: SIGNIFICANT RULING. The Sheikh rules the arrangement to be a loan drawing a benefit, and therefore caught by the prohibition of ribā, and he does so for every variant he lists — prior agreement, lot, need, and monthly request. The English must not blunt this and must not qualify it: he gives no permitted form and no exception.

He does not use the word ḥarām of the practice. He says it is a loan that has drawn a benefit, that 'lend me on condition that I lend you' is a mother-case of ribā, and that it is not lawful to derive worldly benefit from a loan. The English reproduces that chain rather than substituting a one-word verdict.
The closing supplication is part of the text he gave and is translated, not summarised.
